thread:
emily: quick heads-up — after the v5 streaming change landed, we started seeing a handful of prod clients fail to parse frames. low volume but persistent. anyone seen similar?
raj: saw 3 errors in telemetry this morning, all from older mobile SDKs. looks like they assume \"text\" frames only, and v5 introduced \"delta\" envelope.
sam: ugh. we knew this would be a compatibility risk. did we attach a negotiation header?
diana: not by default. v5 docs said clients should handle additional frame types but i guess "should" != reality.
emily: proposed short-term: add a compatibility shim in edge that rewrites v5 frames into the old shape for clients that opt-in via header or user-agent match. long-term: nudge people to opt into v5 shape.
laura: what's the opt-in header? we need something lightweight. maybe `X-Redwood-Stream-Version: 1|5`?
sam: i'd prefer `Accept-Stream-Version: 5` to align with Accept headers. infra-bot: deploy-checklist triggered for shim-proxy v0.2. Will need canary config.
raj: two risk points: (1) transform latency — parsing + re-emit, (2) correctness — we might lose structured delta metadata. can we map deterministically?
diana: most mobile SDKs only use plain text concatenation. we can flatten deltas into text frames for those opt-ins. for advanced clients we preserve full envelope.
emily: plan sketch: 1) edge inspects header or UA whitelist 2) if client indicates legacy, replace {"type":"delta","parts":[...]} with {"type":"text","content":"<concat(parts)>"} 3) record shim metric + tag requests for rollouts
laura: how long a migration window? we should avoid indefinite support. propose 90 days with telemetry gating.
sam: +1 to 90 days. also expose a telemetry dashboard: shim-hit-rate, shim-error-rate, avg extra-latency.
raj: what about signed payloads or encrypted clients? does rewrite break integrity checks?
diana: good call. rewrite will only run on unauthenticated streaming endpoints or when client uses API key with `allow-shim` scope. default: no shim for signed payloads.
emily: can we add an auto-polyfill for clients that are within our mobile SDK versions? e.g., older SDKs automatically get compatibility via UA with no header changes.
laura: need opt-out too — enterprise customers might object. add tenant flag `streaming_compat_mode` in tenant config.
sam: implement in edge service as a tiny stateless transformer. config-driven rules: header, ua regex, tenant flag. canary with 1% of traffic to start. infra-bot: canary group created: edge-canary-compat-v5.
raj: testing: unit tests for mapping logic, e2e against a mocked old SDK that expects text frames, and load tests for latency impact. also a regression test to ensure we don't double-wrap frames.
diana: also capture examples of malformed frames to help SDK teams patch. I'll open a GH issue in mobile-sdk repo with sample payloads.
emily: rollout timeline suggestion: day 0 deploy shim behind feature flag; day 1 enable for UA whitelist; day 7 enable header-based opt-in; day 30 enable tenant opt-in; day 60 telemetry check + notify customers; day 90 turn off default shim and keep opt-in for enterprise for 30 more days then fully sunset.
laura: push notifications + email for top 20 tenants hitting shim. will coordinate comms with growth.
sam: one more thing — function calling uses structured frames. if we flatten deltas we might break tool chaining for legacy clients. need to ensure function call frames either preserved or mapped to fake text stub.
raj: recommend preserving function-call frames only when client indicates it understands structured JSON. otherwise emit a placeholder like `"[function-call-output]"` and log a debug sample.
emily: ok. action items: diana writes transform spec + examples (due EOD), sam prototypes edge transformer (PR next week), raj builds telemetry dashboard (shim metrics + latency), laura drafts comms (customer list + notice). i'll create RFC follow-up note and schedule a 30-min sync Thu.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: make sure canary rollback hook present, add circuit breaker if transformer errors > 0.5% over 5m.
laura: thanks — i'll also include an opt-out support playbook for sales/CS.
diana: starting the spec now. leaving sample payloads in the GH issue.
emily: perfect. if we hit unexpected failure mode we revert flag and notify. :thumbsup:
laura: ack.
raj: ack.
sam: ack.
